paragraphs: The paper studies constrained minimax optimization, where one set of variables seeks to minimize an objective while another seeks to maximize it. Its main setting allows the objective to be nonconvex in the minimizing variables and nonconcave in the maximizing variables. The goal is to reach an approximately stationary point, rather than establish a globally optimal solution.

The proposed single-loop algorithm combines a new extra-gradient difference step with momentum in its dual update. The difference step establishes a mathematical property called quasi-cocoercivity, which supports the improved convergence analysis. The authors obtain this improvement without adding a structural assumption to the constrained nonconvex-nonconcave setting they consider.

For an epsilon-stationary point of the objective f, the stated complexity improves from roughly epsilon to the power minus four to epsilon to the power minus two. The algorithm also achieves the latter rate in the two partially convex special cases. Separately, for the primal function in the nonconvex-concave setting, it improves the previous roughly inverse-cubic bound to an inverse-square bound. These results distinguish guarantees for two different stationarity targets.
neurips-2023-a-single-loop-accelerated-e.tldr: A single-loop minimax algorithm combines an extra-gradient difference step with momentum to improve stated complexity bounds for approximate stationarity.

paragraphs: Federated learning lets several clients train a shared model while keeping their training data local. This paper examines backdoor attacks in that setting, focusing on why a trigger that works on an attacker's local model may become less effective in the shared model. Earlier approaches commonly fixed the trigger or optimized it using only local information.

A3FL adapts the trigger with the wider training process in mind. Its central premise is that differences between local and global models undermine locally optimized triggers. The method therefore optimizes against a worst-case scenario in which the global model is trained specifically to unlearn the trigger. This makes resistance to removal part of the attack objective.

The work targets two weaknesses of previous attacks: limited effectiveness with a restricted attack budget and rapid deterioration after the attacker stops participating. The authors evaluate A3FL on benchmark datasets against twelve existing defenses. The abstract describes this extensive evaluation without reporting numerical outcomes; its central contribution is an attack formulation that explicitly accounts for the global model's changing behavior.
neurips-2023-a3fl-adversarially-adaptive.tldr: A3FL adapts federated-learning backdoor triggers against global-model unlearning to target more durable attacks.

paragraphs: The paper asks whether language models trained to be helpful and harmless preserve that behavior when users deliberately search for inputs that defeat it. The focus is adversarial alignment: whether a model continues to follow its intended restrictions under worst-case inputs designed to elicit otherwise prohibited content.

For text models, the authors find that existing language-based optimization attacks can be too weak to reveal vulnerabilities reliably. They can discover adversarial inputs by brute force even when those attacks fail. This separates two questions that evaluations can conflate: whether an attack succeeds and whether the model is robust. Failure of the tested attack does not establish that the model remains aligned.

The paper also examines multimodal models whose generated text depends on an input image. It reports that adversarial image perturbations can readily induce arbitrary unaligned behavior in the models studied. The authors conjecture that stronger language-based attacks might eventually demonstrate comparable control over text-only models. That extension is a conjecture, whereas the image attacks and the shortcomings of existing text attacks are reported findings.
neurips-2023-are-aligned-neural-networks.tldr: Failed text attacks do not establish adversarial alignment, and the studied multimodal models can be steered into unaligned behavior through image perturbations.

paragraphs: Standard Stackelberg games model a principal choosing an action and an agent responding to it. This paper changes the information available to the agent: the agent cannot directly observe the principal's action and instead responds optimally to calibrated forecasts about it. The principal and agent interact repeatedly, allowing the framework to address decisions based on predictions.

The resulting Calibrated Stackelberg Games avoid requiring one highly specified algorithm for how the agent infers the principal's behavior. The authors also introduce adaptive calibration, a stronger forecasting requirement that gives fine-grained guarantees at arbitrary times against adversarial sequences. They provide a general method for constructing algorithms with this property and specialize it to finite games.

The main result establishes that the principal's utility can converge to the optimal standard Stackelberg value in both finite and continuous settings, and that a higher value is not achievable in this framework. Thus, replacing direct observation with calibrated forecasts preserves the stated optimal utility benchmark. The paper identifies security games and strategic classification against calibrated agents as immediate applications.
neurips-2023-calibrated-stackelberg-game.tldr: A generalized Stackelberg framework shows that a principal can attain the optimal Stackelberg value against agents responding to calibrated forecasts.

paragraphs: ChatIR treats image search as a conversation that can progressively clarify what someone wants. A single description may leave useful details unspecified, so the system asks follow-up questions instead of relying entirely on the initial query. The user's answers provide additional information for finding the desired image in a large collection.

The system uses a large language model to generate those questions. The authors build an evaluation pipeline from an existing manually generated dataset and investigate different system components and training strategies. Their comparisons include strong approaches adapted from related applications and trained with reinforcement learning, allowing them to examine how dialogue design affects retrieval.

In the reported evaluation, ChatIR retrieves the target from 50,000 images with more than 78% success after five dialogue rounds. The corresponding figures are 75% with human-generated questions and 64% for a single text-to-image query. These results support the value of collecting clarifying information through conversation in the tested setting, while the broader evaluation examines performance and limitations across different configurations.
neurips-2023-chatting-makes-perfect-chat.tldr: ChatIR improves image retrieval by using language-model-generated follow-up questions to clarify the user's search.

paragraphs: Computational cognitive models express specific hypotheses about the mechanisms underlying behavior. Building them usually involves researchers repeatedly proposing and refining explanations. This paper explores a data-driven alternative: learning compact cognitive models directly from behavioral observations while keeping their internal representations and dynamics interpretable.

The method fits a recurrent neural network to behavior but penalizes it for carrying excessive information from one time step to the next. This pressure encourages sparse representations and simpler dynamics. The information passed through time is therefore part of the model-discovery problem, rather than an unrestricted resource used only to improve fit.

On synthetic behavior generated by known cognitive models, the method recovers the underlying forms of those models. On choice data from rats performing a bandit task, it produces simple, interpretable models that generate testable predictions about neural mechanisms. The synthetic result demonstrates recovery where the generating model is known; the animal-data result shows how the same approach can propose hypotheses for further testing. The predictions are candidates for investigation, rather than established neural explanations.
neurips-2023-cognitive-model-discovery-v.tldr: Penalizing information carried through a recurrent network yields compact cognitive models that recover known behavioral mechanisms and suggest testable new hypotheses.

paragraphs: A material's density of states describes how its states are distributed across energy levels. Predicting this spectrum therefore requires accounting for both the crystal and the energy at which the spectrum is evaluated. The paper argues that previous work emphasized better crystal representations while overlooking this joint dependence when making predictions.

DOSTransformer combines information about crystalline materials and energies through a multimodal transformer. This lets the prediction model represent complex relationships between atoms and different energy levels. The authors also introduce prompts that guide learning toward interactions specific to the crystal's structural system, bringing that structural distinction into how material and energy information are combined.

The method is evaluated on both phonon and electron density-of-states prediction under several real-world scenarios. The authors report superior performance across their experiments. The contribution centers on how predictions are formed from representations: energy becomes an explicit participant in the model's reasoning about the spectrum. The findings support this joint treatment of structure and energy for the two kinds of spectra studied.
neurips-2023-density-of-states-predictio.tldr: DOSTransformer predicts material spectra by jointly modeling crystal structure and energy levels, guided by structural-system-specific prompts.

paragraphs: The paper studies contextual bandits in which a learner chooses among K actions using d-dimensional contextual information, while action losses can change arbitrarily over time. Regret measures the learner's cumulative disadvantage relative to a comparison policy. With contexts drawn from a fixed, known distribution, the established worst-case expected regret scales roughly as the square root of K times d times T.

The authors derive more adaptive guarantees under the additional assumption that the context distribution has a log-concave density. One bound depends on the cumulative second moment of the learner's losses, V_T; another depends on the best policy's cumulative loss, L_T*. Their respective orders are K times the square root of d V_T and K times the square root of d L_T*, ignoring logarithmic factors.

These quantities can be substantially smaller than the number of rounds, so the bounds can improve on worst-case guarantees in sufficiently benign environments. The algorithm uses a truncated continuous exponential-weights procedure over action probabilities. Its analysis connects the contextual problem to linear bandits without contexts, providing a route to loss-sensitive guarantees.
neurips-2023-first-and-second-order-boun.tldr: Under a known log-concave context distribution, new contextual-bandit regret bounds adapt to losses and can improve guarantees in benign environments.

paragraphs: Representation learning is widely used when reinforcement-learning agents receive images, but this paper focuses on environments described by low-level state variables. Physical control is one such setting. The authors argue that useful learned representations can still matter here, especially when they capture how a state and a chosen action interact.

SALE learns embeddings designed to represent that interaction. The paper studies different embedding designs and identifies considerations that affect their effectiveness. The authors then combine SALE with an adaptation of checkpoints for reinforcement learning inside TD3, producing the TD7 algorithm. The evaluated algorithm therefore incorporates both state-action representation learning and the checkpoint adaptation.

On OpenAI Gym benchmark tasks, TD7 reports average performance gains over TD3 of 276.7% at 300,000 time steps and 50.7% at five million time steps. It also works in both online and offline settings and is reported to outperform existing continuous-control algorithms significantly. These findings support learning representations even when observations already consist of low-level states, rather than reserving that approach for image inputs.
neurips-2023-for-sale-state-action-repre.tldr: SALE learns state-action embeddings that, together with adapted checkpointing in TD7, substantially improve reported continuous-control performance.

paragraphs: Unsupervised skill discovery aims to learn useful behaviors without an external reward specifying each one. These behaviors can subsequently be combined to address harder tasks. Extending this idea to multiple agents creates two connected problems: learning skills that describe a whole team's behavior as well as individual behavior, and coordinating which skills different agents use.

Hierarchical Multi-Agent Skill Discovery addresses these problems with two policy levels. A transformer-based high-level policy assigns skills sequentially. A low-level policy learns valuable skills for both individual agents and the team. This division gives the method an explicit mechanism for coordinating skill assignments alongside a mechanism for discovering the behaviors those assignments invoke.

The authors evaluate HMASD on multi-agent benchmarks with sparse rewards and report significant gains over strong multi-agent reinforcement-learning baselines. The findings support the usefulness of combining team-level and individual skill discovery with hierarchical coordination in those tasks. They also connect the two challenges directly: discovering a repertoire of behaviors is paired with learning how to deploy it across agents.
neurips-2023-hierarchical-multi-agent-sk.tldr: HMASD discovers individual and team skills and coordinates them hierarchically, improving performance on sparse-reward multi-agent benchmarks.

paragraphs: Best-arm identification concerns deciding which option has the highest mean using measurements of the available options. The knowledge gradient algorithm chooses each measurement according to its expected one-step improvement in the estimated best mean. This paper shows that this criterion has limitations that prevent the algorithm from being asymptotically optimal.

The proposed improved knowledge gradient, or iKG, preserves the one-step look-ahead approach but changes the quantity it seeks to improve. It chooses measurements for their expected improvement in the probability of selecting the best arm. This connects measurement selection more directly to the final identification decision, rather than to the numerical estimate of the best mean.

The authors show that iKG is asymptotically optimal. They also find it easier to extend than KG to related identification tasks, illustrating this with epsilon-good arm identification and feasible arm identification. Numerical examples demonstrate superior performance on these problems. The theoretical result concerns asymptotic behavior, while the numerical studies provide separate evidence for the practical value of changing the one-step objective.
neurips-2023-improving-the-knowledge-gra.tldr: iKG improves best-arm identification by choosing measurements that increase the probability of selecting the best option, yielding asymptotic optimality.

paragraphs: Object-centric learning seeks structured representations that separate objects within visual data without requiring object labels. Video offers information about how content changes over time, but previous methods had reached real-world video mainly in restricted domains. This paper builds on findings that reconstructing pretrained self-supervised features can support object discovery in unconstrained images.

The proposed temporal feature similarity loss uses those pretrained features to capture relationships between image patches across time. It incorporates both semantic similarity and temporal correlations, introducing a preference for using motion information during object discovery. The learning signal therefore draws on how features relate across a video, in addition to what individual frames contain.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on the challenging synthetic MOVi datasets. Combining temporal similarity with feature reconstruction also allows their model to scale to unconstrained video collections such as YouTube-VIS, which they describe as a first for object-centric video models. The two findings address distinct settings: strong synthetic benchmark results and a demonstrated expansion to less restricted real-world video.
neurips-2023-object-centric-learning-for.tldr: Predicting temporal similarities between pretrained features improves unsupervised object discovery and helps it scale to unconstrained real-world video.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning learns decision policies from previously collected data. In applications involving sensitive records, the resulting policy may retain information about individuals, including their treatments and outcomes. This paper addresses privacy at the level of the learning algorithm, so that producing a useful policy also comes with a formal privacy guarantee.

The authors design offline reinforcement-learning algorithms with differential privacy guarantees and establish learning bounds that depend on the particular problem instance. Their analysis covers both tabular Markov decision processes and linear Markov decision processes. These results connect the privacy protection to guarantees about how well the algorithms learn within the two settings studied.

The theory and simulations suggest that, for a medium-size dataset, the privacy guarantee can come with almost no reduction in utility relative to a non-private counterpart. This is a qualified finding about the analyzed and simulated settings, rather than a claim that privacy is always cost-free. Its significance is that formal privacy protection and useful offline policy learning can coexist with a small observed or predicted utility penalty.
neurips-2023-offline-reinforcement-learn.tldr: Differentially private offline-RL algorithms achieve instance-dependent learning guarantees, with theory and simulations suggesting almost no utility loss for medium-size datasets.

paragraphs: Data acquisition decisions often have to be made after seeing only a small sample from each prospective source. The paper addresses how to predict model performance for different source mixtures and larger purchases under this partial visibility. Existing performance-scaling approaches can be expensive to fit, susceptible to overfitting, or difficult to use for selection.

The proposed framework, projektor, separates prediction into two stages. First, it uses optimal transport distance to predict performance across mixture ratios within the range of disclosed data sizes. Second, a parameter-free mapping inspired by neural scaling laws extrapolates those predictions to larger, undisclosed sizes. A gradient-based selection method then uses projected performance to choose data sources.

Evaluations cover applications including vision, text, fine-tuning, and noisy sources. The authors report improvements in prediction accuracy and the computational cost of constructing the predictor, together with substantially better data selection than the compared off-the-shelf methods. The approach links predictions made from limited previews to a concrete selection procedure, making those predictions directly useful for choosing a data mixture.
neurips-2023-performance-scaling-via-opt.tldr: Projektor combines optimal-transport-based performance prediction with scaling extrapolation to select data sources from limited previews.

paragraphs: Estimating a probability distribution can be difficult when its formula is known only up to a normalization constant that is expensive to compute. Score matching avoids computing that constant by fitting the distribution's score. This paper asks whether that computational advantage can be established rigorously without giving up the statistical efficiency associated with maximum likelihood.

The authors identify a natural exponential family whose members are exponentials of fixed-degree polynomials. For this family, they show that providing either function-value or first-order access for optimizing the maximum-likelihood loss is NP-hard. Maximum likelihood nevertheless has statistical efficiency polynomial in the ambient dimension and the radius of the family's parameters, separating statistical feasibility from computational accessibility.

For the same family, minimizing the score-matching loss is both computationally and statistically efficient, with complexity polynomial in the ambient dimension. The result supplies a concrete case where score matching offers a provable computational benefit while retaining comparable statistical efficiency. Its scope is the constructed family; the contribution establishes that this favorable tradeoff exists, rather than asserting it for all distribution-estimation problems.
neurips-2023-provable-benefits-of-score-.tldr: For a fixed-degree polynomial exponential family, score matching is efficiently optimizable with statistical efficiency comparable to computationally intractable maximum likelihood.

paragraphs: Regret Matching+ is widely used to solve large games, but its practical success has lacked a matching theoretical explanation. Many recent fast-convergence results rely on learning algorithms being stable. This paper shows through counterexamples that Regret Matching+ and its predictive variant can be unstable, potentially causing other players to accumulate large regret.

The authors propose two stabilizing modifications: restarting the procedure and trimming the positive orthant in which its updates operate. They prove these changes are sufficient for predictive Regret Matching+ to achieve individual regret of order T to the one-quarter power and constant-order social regret in normal-form games. The distinction matters because the guarantees describe both individual behavior and regret aggregated across players.

The paper also applies its stabilization techniques to clairvoyant updates in an uncoupled learning setting, obtaining guarantees similar to those established for clairvoyant online mirror descent. Experiments in matrix and extensive-form games show advantages over unmodified Regret Matching+ variants. Together, the counterexamples, repairs, and evaluations connect a specific source of instability to improved theoretical and empirical behavior.
neurips-2023-regret-matching-in-stabilit.tldr: Regret Matching+ can be unstable, but two stabilizing modifications yield stronger regret guarantees and empirical improvements.

paragraphs: CLIP can struggle when moved from natural images into specialist domains where paired images and captions are scarce. S-CLIP adapts the model using a small paired collection together with additional images that have no captions. Its central contribution is to turn those unpaired images into useful training examples through two complementary forms of pseudo-labeling.

At the caption level, an optimal transport problem connects unpaired and paired images, producing supervision from combinations of existing captions. At the keyword level, supervision comes from keywords in the caption of the nearest paired image. Partial-label learning handles this second signal through candidate labels, rather than requiring one exact label to be known.

Combining the two objectives improves training across remote sensing, fashion, scientific figures, and comics. On the remote-sensing benchmark, the authors report a 10% improvement in zero-shot classification and a 4% improvement in image-text retrieval over CLIP. S-CLIP also matches supervised CLIP there with three times fewer image-text pairs, demonstrating the value of exploiting images that lack specialist captions.
neurips-2023-s-clip-semi-supervised-visi.tldr: S-CLIP uses caption- and keyword-level pseudo-labels to adapt CLIP to specialist domains with few paired captions and additional unpaired images.

paragraphs: Gradient-based meta-learning learns through an inner optimization process that adapts model parameters. This paper proposes that such methods implicitly suppress the Hessian along that adaptation trajectory. The Hessian describes how gradients change around the current parameters, so the hypothesis concerns the curvature encountered during learning, rather than only the final parameter values.

SHOT turns this hypothesis into an explicit algorithm by minimizing the distance between the parameters of a target model and a reference model. This objective is intended to suppress the Hessian during the inner loop. Although it addresses higher-order quantities, the authors report that it adds relatively little computational complexity to the underlying method.

The method is described as independent of the particular gradient-based meta-learning algorithm and architecture. Tests on standard few-shot learning tasks show improvements over the corresponding baselines, while qualitative analysis examines the learning dynamics. The authors report empirical confirmation of their hypothesis. The evidence therefore supports the proposed curvature-related explanation experimentally, alongside demonstrating the usefulness of the resulting training modification.
neurips-2023-shot-suppressing-the-hessia.tldr: SHOT explicitly encourages Hessian suppression during meta-learning adaptation and improves the tested few-shot baselines with modest added complexity.

paragraphs: Learning theory contains many definitions of stability, making it difficult to see which capture distinct requirements and which express related guarantees. This paper develops a more systematic organization by dividing Bayesian stability into two families: definitions that depend on the data distribution and definitions that are distribution-independent.

Within each family, the authors establish equivalences among a range of stability notions. These encompass pure and approximate differential privacy, replicability, global stability, perfect generalization, and stability measured through total variation, mutual information, KL divergence, and Rényi divergence. The family distinction is central to the result: the abstract states equivalences within each family, rather than identifying all definitions across both families.

The paper also proves boosting results that amplify the stability of a learning rule. This adds a constructive component to the taxonomy, showing how stability can be strengthened as well as how its definitions relate. The contribution is a set of mathematical connections that helps clarify a crowded conceptual landscape and supports a more unified understanding of guarantees previously described using different terminology.
neurips-2023-the-bayesian-stability-zoo-.tldr: The paper establishes equivalences within two families of Bayesian stability notions and proves methods for amplifying stability.

paragraphs: Filtering and smoothing in high-dimensional dynamical systems become expensive when they require full covariance matrices. This paper proposes an approximate Gaussian method that carries low-rank covariance representations through the computation. The aim is to reduce the cost of tracking uncertainty while retaining a controlled connection to the exact Kalman filter.

During prediction, the method projects the relevant Lyapunov equations onto a space of low-rank matrices and solves them with a numerically stable dynamical low-rank integrator. During updates, it exploits the fact that the covariance update transforms the matrix's column space, which is already low-rank. Unlike ensemble approaches, these approximations are deterministic.

As the retained dimension approaches the full problem dimension, the method can reproduce the exact Kalman filter. Its worst-case computational complexity is quadratic in state-space size rather than cubic, and becomes linear when the model satisfies additional criteria. In data-assimilation and spatio-temporal regression experiments, it consistently produces smaller mean and covariance errors relative to the exact filter than ensemble methods, without increasing asymptotic computational complexity.
neurips-2023-the-rank-reduced-kalman-fil.tldr: A deterministic low-rank Kalman approximation reduces computational cost and improves reported accuracy over ensemble methods.

paragraphs: Stein Variational Gradient Descent represents distributions through deterministically moving particles, but its theoretical behavior can be difficult to characterize. The paper studies a Gaussian version built using a bilinear kernel. A motivating property is that, for a Gaussian target and Gaussian initialization, the resulting distribution dynamics remain Gaussian.

The analysis covers both a continuous mean-field description and systems with finitely many particles. For a strongly log-concave target, the mean-field dynamics converge linearly to the Gaussian distribution closest to the target in KL divergence. For a Gaussian target, the finite-particle results include uniform-in-time convergence to the mean-field limit and linear convergence over time to equilibrium.

For more general targets, the authors develop both density-based and particle-based implementations. Their framework also recovers several recent Gaussian variational-inference algorithms as special cases, connecting methods developed from different viewpoints. One new particle-based instance empirically outperforms existing approaches. The work therefore combines conditional convergence guarantees, a unifying formulation, and an experimentally promising algorithm, with the Gaussian approximation family remaining central to the analysis.
neurips-2023-towards-understanding-the-d.tldr: Gaussian-SVGD receives conditional convergence guarantees and a unified framework that connects several Gaussian variational-inference methods.

paragraphs: Large-scale image retrieval needs compact representations that support efficient approximate nearest-neighbor search. Deep hashing is promising, but the paper argues that evaluation on relatively small datasets can conceal problems that appear as categories and samples multiply. Those problems include excessive training costs and inadequate retrieval accuracy.

The authors propose a deep hashing framework based on product quantization. A softmax-based differentiable branch learns a set of predefined class-level product-quantization codes. The approach is designed to produce compact codes that distinguish classes well without requiring large-scale matrix operations. This directly addresses the joint challenge of representation quality and computational demands during training.

Evaluation spans ImageNet100, ImageNet1K, and Glint360K, with category counts ranging from 100 to 360,000 and sample counts from 10,000 to 17 million. The authors report superior performance across extensive experiments. Testing across these scales is a substantive part of the contribution: the proposed method is assessed in settings that expose the growth in classes and data motivating its design, rather than only on small retrieval collections.
neurips-2023-unleashing-the-full-potenti.tldr: A differentiable product-quantization framework learns compact image-retrieval codes and reports strong results on datasets reaching 17 million samples.

paragraphs: Judging how well a caption fits an image involves subjective choices, making reliable evaluation difficult. The Validated Image Caption Rating dataset addresses this problem by improving how human judgments are collected. Its contribution combines a new rating resource with a rating system intended to make judgments more consistent and teachable.

The system uses a newly designed robust rating scale and a gamified process for collecting responses. A total of 113 participants contribute 68,217 ratings covering 15,646 image-caption pairs. The authors show that people can learn the rating approach and apply it consistently, supporting the usefulness of the resulting judgments as evaluation data.

The dataset achieves greater agreement among raters than the previous state of the art. Relative to Flickr8k-Expert, the reported improvements are 12% in Kendall's W and 19% in Fleiss' kappa, two measures used to assess agreement. Custom machine-learning rating predictors trained on VICR also outperform previous metrics. These findings connect the collection method to both more consistent human evaluation and improved automated prediction of caption ratings.
neurips-2023-validated-image-caption-rat.tldr: VICR combines a teachable rating scale with gamified annotation to improve agreement on caption quality and train stronger rating predictors.

paragraphs: Text-guided editing of a three-dimensional scene must keep the requested changes consistent when the scene is viewed from different directions. ViCA-NeRF addresses this by explicitly sharing editing information across views, alongside the scene representation supplied by a neural radiance field. The method combines geometric relationships with learned image representations to coordinate the edits.

Its geometric regularization uses depth from the NeRF to establish correspondences between views. Its learned regularization aligns latent codes from a two-dimensional diffusion model between edited and unedited images. Together, these mechanisms allow edits made to key views to propagate throughout the scene, linking appearance changes to both scene geometry and learned visual information.

The process has two stages: blending edits from multiple views into a preliminary three-dimensional result, then training the NeRF further to refine its appearance. Experiments report more flexible editing, greater consistency and detail, and a threefold speed improvement over the state of the art. These results support explicit cross-view propagation as a way to improve both the coherence and efficiency of scene editing.
neurips-2023-vica-nerf-view-consistency-.tldr: ViCA-NeRF propagates text-guided edits across views using geometry and diffusion-model representations, improving reported consistency, detail, and speed.

paragraphs: Vision foundation models often perform tasks in predefined forms, while language models can accept more flexible instructions. VisionLLM explores how to bring that instruction-driven flexibility to vision tasks. It uses a language-model-based framework in which the task definition can be expressed and adjusted through language.

The framework treats images as another language and aligns vision tasks with language tasks. An LLM-based decoder then produces predictions according to the supplied instructions. The authors investigate customization at different scales, from instructions concerning particular objects to instructions defining a broader task. This makes the instruction part of specifying what the model should predict.

Experiments show good results across these levels of customization. The model also exceeds 60% mean average precision on COCO, placing its reported detection performance on par with detection-specific models despite using a generalist framework. That result links flexibility with a concrete vision benchmark: the paper demonstrates that an instruction-driven LLM decoder can support task customization while retaining competitive detection performance in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2023-visionllm-large-language-mo.tldr: VisionLLM uses a language-model decoder for instruction-customizable vision tasks while reporting detection performance comparable to specialized models.
